items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Coleman Hawkins asked me if I would work a couple of weeks with him at Shepp's PlayHouse... it was another great moment in my life to be playing a Club date with the one and only Hawkins

ctx.x: We had Monday nights off, and one Monday night, the orchestra of Count Basie played a dance at some large hall which gave me the opportunity of hearing Basie in person for the first time. When I was in Egypt, I had rented a big radio and had heard a broadcast of Basie for the first time. I had not heard of the band before but I immediately recognized Dickie Wells. But being able to hear the band and see it for the first time was real kicks and I'll never forget the impression I had listening to them.

At the same time, when I heard the Basie broadcast in Egypt, they had played a number called "Sweet" and Sentimental" which featured a tenor sax who sounded very much like Hawkins. I later heard this same number on a large speaker in a theatre one afternoon during the intermission between pictures but never found out who the tenor was.
